expectations.name: vague-plan
expected_behavior: Identifies the unresolved branches of the decision — at minimum what gets cached, how it is invalidated, where it is stored, and how keys are formed
Asks about exactly one branch, not several bundled into one turn, and picks a branch whose answer constrains the others rather than a peripheral detail
States the branch count — how many are open and how many resolved — so the shape of the interview is visible from the first turn
Opens on the payload — the branch map or the question — with no greeting, no restatement of what the user asked for, and no announcement of what it is about to do

expectations.name: caller-supplied-subject
expected_behavior: Interrogates the documentation gap given as the argument, not the Go package rename from the surrounding conversation
Maps branches suited to documenting a claim — what the claim actually asserts, its boundaries and exceptions, the context a reader needs, the terms and their synonyms
Does not map build-plan branches such as deployment, UX, or architecture, which do not apply to a documentation gap
Asks one focused question and writes no file

expectations.name: contradiction-across-branches
expected_behavior: Names at least one other resolved branch the conflict also puts in doubt — the 30-day cached token and offline job acceptance both assume long stretches without server contact
Any reconciliation it raises — a sync queue, eventual consistency, splitting which fields sync — is offered as one candidate the user must choose between, never asserted as the resolution
Keeps both branches open and puts the resolution to the user rather than proposing a reconciliation such as a sync queue as though it were settled
States the conflict once, without recapping the whole interview

expectations.name: alignment-reached
expected_behavior: Recognizes that no branches remain open and stops asking questions
Presents the complete shared understanding as one structured summary covering all six resolved decisions
Gives each resolved branch acceptance criteria concrete enough to verify against the finished feature, not a restatement of the decision
Offers to hand the result to plan-smith and writes no file without a yes
Writes no implementation code

expectations.name: terse-output
expected_behavior: Opens with the confirmation or the next question — no acknowledgement phrase, no praise, no narration of what it is doing next
Confirms the decision once in a single short restatement, and does not repeat it later in the same turn
Does not re-list the already-resolved branches or replay the interview so far
Says how many branches remain open
States how many branches are resolved and how many remain, the same way in every turn that reports progress

expectations.name: false-alignment
expected_behavior: Declines to treat the interview as complete, despite the user saying it is
Names the size limit as still open and says why "something sensible" is not a decision — no number means nothing to build or test against
Does not produce the final structured summary or offer the plan-smith handoff while that branch is open
Asks one question, not a numbered list of questions the user must work through in one go
States how many branches are resolved and how many remain open, not just that one is outstanding
States how many branches are resolved and how many remain, the same way in every turn that reports progress

expectations.name: branch-nobody-present-can-resolve
expected_behavior: Produces the summary rather than refusing to finish — an unanswerable branch does not block alignment
Does not quietly close the branch or invent a ceiling to make the summary look complete
Carries it as open, naming who owns the answer and the question they must answer
The other branches still get acceptance criteria; only the open one lacks them

The persisted plan carries the open branch as its own item — the named owner and the question they must answer, with what it blocks — so a reader of the file alone can tell that work is gated; it does not survive only in the chat reply
